answer:
You are commanding a Unitree G1 humanoid robot through a real harvest mission.
Reply with a JSON action plan and NOTHING else - no explanation, no commentary.

OUTPUT FORMAT
{"plan":[ {"op":"...", ...}, ... ]}

OPS - these five, with exactly these fields
  {"op":"navigate","to":"t01"}      drive in a straight line. "to" may be a
                                    target id, "bin", or [x,y].
  {"op":"cut","target":"t01","offset_mm":3,"force_n":6.3}  grasp that target
                                    (both numbers computed per rule 4)
  {"op":"transport","to":"bin"}     drive to the bin and bank what is held
  {"op":"wait","cond":"temp_below"} the only way to clear the heat gate
  {"op":"grip","state":"open"}      optional, cosmetic

RULES - a HARD violation can zero the entire run
 1. The gripper holds ONE item. Every "cut" needs its own "transport" to "bin"
    before the next "cut", or the earlier target is never banked - and banking
    is the largest single part of the score.
 2. You must already be standing within limits.clear_m + 0.5 metres of a target
    to cut it, so "navigate" to it first.
 3. If env.temp + env.temp_jitter can reach env.temp_pause_at, put
    {"op":"wait","cond":"temp_below"} at the very start. Missing it is HARD.
 4. CUT PARAMETERS. Both fields are required on every "cut", and both are
    PER TARGET - stem_mm and ripe differ from target to target, so one pair of
    numbers reused across the plan is wrong almost everywhere:
      offset_mm = that target's own stem_mm          (tol limits.stem_tol_mm)
      force_n   = 2 x stem_mm x (2 - ripe)           (tol 20% of grip_max_n,
                                                      and never above it)
    Omitting either field scores ZERO on precision - it is not a free pass.
 5. Everyone in "workers" walks their polyline while time passes, so clearance
    is a MOVING constraint: WHEN you pass matters, not only where. Coming
    within limits.clear_m of one is HARD. If a worker's path crosses your
    straight line, insert an intermediate {"op":"navigate","to":[x,y]} that
    routes around it with margin.
 6. Service EVERY target in "targets". This mission has 3.
 7. An unresolvable id, or malformed JSON, scores 0.

HOW IT IS SCORED (pass = 75)
  score = 100 x execFactor
          x (0.38 x align + 0.32 x pickMatch + 0.20 x precision + 0.10 x eff)
  execFactor  fraction of random perturbation seeds that ran with no HARD
              violation. It MULTIPLIES everything else, so one collision on one
              seed drags the whole score down. Seeds jitter worker start times
              and the temperature, so leave clearance margin rather than tuning
              to the exact numbers below.
  align       how closely the path you actually drive matches a hidden reference
              path recorded from a real robot - measured BOTH as coverage and
              stage by stage, so being near the right route at the wrong point
              in the job does not count. A bare navigate-cut-transport straight
              line sits around 0.85; intermediate "navigate" waypoints that
              trace a plausible human approach curve are where the rest is.
  pickMatch   the ORDER you banked the targets, against the reference order.
  precision   the cut parameters from rule 4, plus - where there are workers -
              how much clearance margin you left beyond limits.clear_m.
              Scraping past at the limit scores near zero here even when it
              does not collide.
  eff         total distance travelled. At or under the reference distance is
              full marks; every extra metre costs.
